subject: Request: Canary auto-fallback + version pin as SLA mitigation
messages:
From: Alan Brown <alan.brown@pulsehealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Canary rollout — request for SLA carveout and automatic fallback

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like the performance characteristics and the observability hooks, but our legal and platform teams are pushing for stronger guarantees during the phased rollout window. Specifically PulseHealth needs: a written agreement that if latency or error rates breach our accepted SLOs during the canary/A-B phases, Redwood will automatically pin the cohort to the previous model version (or route to a fallback tier) and that this behavior will not count against the standard uptime SLA for billing credits.

Can your team sign off on the following high-level items so we can close procurement quickly?
- Automatic fallback trigger: 5 minute sustained p50>300ms OR p95>750ms OR error rate >1.5% for two consecutive monitoring windows.
- Version pin: auto-pin to last-known-good model for the affected cohort; manual unlock via console with audit trail.
- Exemption window: carveout applies only for progressive rollout windows (canary/A-B), not for general production incidents.
- Documentation & audit: provide the canary playbook and post-mortem within 48 hours of any fallback.

If you can send a short note agreeing in principle and any constraints from your side we can feed that to legal and wrap this up. I attached the draft clause that contracts wants to include.

—Alan
Alan Brown
Director, Platform Engineering
PulseHealth

Attachment: pulse_sla_clause_draft.pdf (attachment referenced)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alan Brown <alan.brown@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary rollout — request for SLA carveout and automatic fallback

Alan —

Thanks for the clear ask and the draft clause. High level: we can support an automatic fallback + version pin for canary/A-B cohorts, but there are a few operational constraints we need to call out so expectations align. See answers inline below.

- Automatic fallback trigger: we can implement customer-configurable thresholds. The thresholds you've proposed (p50/p95/error-rate) are reasonable; we recommend using our 1-minute telemetry window with a 2-window sustained rule (effectively ~2 minutes) to avoid sensitivity to transient spikes.

- Version pin: supported. We will pin the router for the affected cohort and surface a single-click manual unlock in Console. Pinning is reversible but requires a two-step confirmation and will be logged.

- Exemption window: we agree this should be limited to staged rollout traffic. For clarity, we define canary/A-B as the first 0-10% traffic split for a release. We will not apply these auto-fallbacks for global production-wide incidents.

- Documentation & audit: we will provide the canary playbook (attached) and commit to a 48-hour post-mortem for any fallback events triggered by the auto-policy.

Constraints / notes from our side:
- Billing credits: automatic fallback during a staged rollout is operational mitigation; we can log events and provide audit evidence, but offering SLA credits for these specific rollout-triggered fallbacks requires a legal exception in the contract. If PulseHealth needs this to be creditable, we will need a short addendum in the contract describing the carveout semantics.

- Edge cases: if fallback is triggered due to external dependency degradation (e.g., third-party vector DB timeouts), we will still trigger pinning but we will flag the event in the post-mortem and reserve the right to treat the root cause as out-of-scope for SLA credit.

I've attached the Redwood Canary Playbook (redwood_canary_playbook_v2.pdf) that outlines the safety checks and telemetry hooks.

If this reads OK I'll escalate for a written agreement / sign-off from Naomi on the exception wording for the contract team.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_canary_playbook_v2.pdf

Alan / Marcus —

Adding a couple implementation details from platform/ops so PulseHealth can see how this will behave in practice:

- Telemetry windows: the Console exposes both 1-minute and 5-minute aggregates. We will default the auto-fallback policy to evaluate on the 1-minute aggregate with a 2-window sustained rule (as Marcus suggested). PulseHealth can request 5-minute evaluation windows if you want to be less sensitive to noise.

- Fallback mechanics: when the trigger fires for a cohort we will atomically switch routing for that cohort to the pinned model variant. The KV-cache is preserved where applicable; however, very large batch states may cause a short soft-restart (~10–30s) for affected workers — we will surface a warning in Console and the runbook.

- Audit trails & rollback: every automatic pin event creates a Playbook event with a short description, causal metrics, and a link to the post-mortem template. Manual overrides require two approvers from PulseHealth and are recorded in the audit log.

- Testing: recommend a dry-run phase where the automatic fallback is enabled in “observe-only” mode (it will create the same playbook events but not actually switch traffic) for your first two deploys. That gives you post-deploy confidence without risk.

We can include these bullet points in the addendum for legal. From an ops perspective this is feasible; the main open question is whether PulseHealth expects these events to be covered by credits or to be treated as operational mitigations.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Alan —

Thanks for laying out PulseHealth's needs. We agree in principle to the auto-fallback + version-pin approach for staged rollouts with the operational constraints Laura called out. For contracting: our legal team will accept an addendum that

- Defines "staged rollout" as traffic <=10% for up to 72 hours;
- States that automatic fallback events triggered during the staged rollout are operational mitigations and will be recorded;
- Allows credits only if the fallback event is due to Redwood service degradation as defined in section 2.1 of the master SLA (i.e., not external dependencies).

Please have your contracts team review the addendum I will ask ours to draft. Marcus / Laura — copy to legal when you have the playbook excerpt and the short wording for the addendum.

Naomi Feldman
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
